lawmakers.name: Rep. Neal Dunn
lawmakers.summary: Primary sponsor of H.R. 906, the REPAIR Act. A physician by background, Dunn frames right-to-repair as a consumer rights issue — owners of complex equipment deserve access to their own diagnostic data.

lawmakers.name: Sen. Maria Cantwell
lawmakers.summary: Senate sponsor of the Stop Motorcycle Profiling Act. Washington State was the first in the nation to pass anti-profiling protections for motorcyclists in 2011 — Cantwell is trying to make that federal policy.

lawmakers.name: Rep. Adam Smith
lawmakers.summary: House companion sponsor of the Stop Motorcycle Profiling Act. Has introduced this bill in multiple congresses — persistence is building bipartisan awareness of the issue.

lawmakers.name: Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
lawmakers.summary: Co-owner of an auto repair shop before entering Congress. Gluesenkamp Perez has been the most vocal champion of right-to-repair in the House — she understands the dealer data lockout problem from personal experience.

lawmakers.name: Rep. Brett Guthrie
lawmakers.summary: Chair of the House Energy & Commerce Committee — the committee the REPAIR Act must clear before a full House vote. Guthrie controls the hearing schedule. Has not publicly committed to advancing the bill. His position on right-to-repair will determine whether H.R. 906 gets a hearing in 2026.
industry_flags: Received contributions from automotive manufacturer PACs

lawmakers.name: Rep. Frank Pallone
lawmakers.summary: Ranking Democrat on House Energy & Commerce. Pallone has been supportive of right-to-repair framing on consumer rights grounds. His support gives the REPAIR Act bipartisan committee backing — meaningful for any bill trying to move in a divided Congress.

lawmakers.name: Sen. Ted Cruz
lawmakers.summary: Chair of Senate Commerce, Science & Transportation — the committee that would handle a Senate version of the REPAIR Act and any federal motorcycle rights legislation. Cruz has not taken a public position on right-to-repair. His committee is the bottleneck for any Senate movement.

lawmakers.name: Sen. John Cornyn
lawmakers.summary: Senior member of Senate Judiciary, which handles the Stop Motorcycle Profiling Act. Texas has a large and active riding community — Cornyn has not engaged publicly on the profiling bill despite his constituency having a direct stake.

lawmakers.name: Rep. Bob Latta
lawmakers.summary: Senior Republican on Energy & Commerce and cosponsor of the REPAIR Act. Latta's inside-committee backing gives the bill Republican credibility where it counts — inside the room where the hearing schedule gets set.

lawmakers.name: Rep. Suzan DelBene
lawmakers.summary: Cosponsor of the REPAIR Act. Represents a tech-forward district where constituents are keenly aware of software-locked devices. Her support broadens the coalition beyond traditional auto and powersports constituencies.

lawmakers.name: Rep. Michael McCaul
lawmakers.summary: Has not cosponsored the REPAIR Act despite representing a large Texas district with a significant riding community. Received documented contributions from automotive manufacturer PACs that are actively lobbying against H.R. 906.
industry_flags: Automotive manufacturer PAC contributions — industry actively opposes REPAIR Act

lawmakers.name: Rep. Lisa Blunt Rochester
lawmakers.summary: Sits on Senate Commerce and has not engaged on the Stop Motorcycle Profiling Act despite being a co-chair of the Congressional Black Caucus — the group most acutely affected by pretextual traffic stops. Her position is being watched by the MRF.

industry_influence.motivation: Dealer service networks generate significant revenue. Open telematics access threatens the dealer data monopoly.
industry_influence.rider_signal: When an OEM donates to a lawmaker, watch that lawmaker's position on H.R. 906.

industry_influence.motivation: Authorized dealers benefit directly from OEM data lockout — it forces customers into their service bays.
industry_influence.rider_signal: Dealer association lobbying is often more effective than OEM lobbying because dealers have local relationships with every member of Congress.

industry_influence.motivation: Universal helmet laws correlate with reduced fatality claims. Insurers fund safety advocacy aligned with their actuarial interests.
industry_influence.rider_signal: Insurance industry lobbying for helmet mandates is well-funded and bipartisan. ABATE and AMA counter this at the state level.

industry_influence.motivation: Open data access means independent shops can compete on equal footing with dealer service departments.
industry_influence.rider_signal: The Auto Care Association's lobbying arm is the primary industry coalition pushing H.R. 906 alongside the AMA.

industry_influence.examples: American Motorcyclist Association, Motorcycle Riders Foundation
industry_influence.position: PRO rider rights across all issues
industry_influence.motivation: Member-funded advocacy organizations with no corporate conflicts. Positions reflect rider membership votes.
industry_influence.rider_signal: These are your orgs. When they send an action alert, respond.
